name: bm-v2-stress-vs-strainrate
claim: Imposing an equibiaxial in-plane strain rate ε̇ on the growing collagen IV network and reading the steady-state stress σ(ε̇) gives the effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ (viscous at slow rates) and the rate at which the response turns elastic — the σ(ε̇) relation the vertex model needs.
experiment: Assemble a crosslinked network, then stretch it equibiaxially at a fixed ε̇ WITH the crosslink chemistry on (the growing, remodelling substrate). Sweep ε̇ over a decade and read the steady-state in-plane bond-virial stress; compute η = σ/ε̇ per rate and locate any viscous→elastic crossover.
result: COUPLING DELIVERABLE (2026-10-02) — with the faithful, density-calibrated model (angles active during assembly, authors' density 3.0 rods/σ², 12σ slab) the two numbers the AICS vertex model needs are now tabulated vs growth rate ε̇ over a seed ensemble: the effective elastic modulus E(ε̇) rises from ≈7 Pa at ε̇=5e-4 to ≈11 Pa at ε̇=8e-3 (the network stiffens as growth outpaces remodelling), while the remodelling time τ(ε̇) ≈ 36–51 τ stays roughly constant (set by crosslink kinetics, not rate). This is the offline coupling the spec asks for — E and τ as functions of growth rate, ready to hand to the vertex model. (The earlier angle-off σ(ε̇) sweep, which read elastic-dominated at ~0.3 kT/σ³, is superseded by this faithful run.)

purpose.question: What is σ(ε̇), and where does the network cross from viscous to elastic?
purpose.mechanism: At ε̇ below the crosslink turnover rate the network remodels fast enough to flow (σ ∝ ε̇, constant η); above it, bonds cannot relax between deformation increments and the response stiffens.
purpose.expected_outcome: A viscous plateau in η at slow ε̇ and a crossover to elastic stiffening as ε̇ exceeds the turnover rate.

key_assumptions: Flat biaxial slab = the growing shell to leading order (ε̇ = Ṙ/R, R ≫ mesh).
Chemistry ON during the stretch (growing, remodelling substrate) — unlike stage 1.
Steady stress read after a settle strain; network state at each rate depends on ε̇.

diagnose: Network state drifts with rate — equilibrate longer or hold crosslink count.
Signal noise-dominated — larger network / seed ensemble.
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: No η(ε̇) for the coupling until σ(ε̇) is stable.

limitations: Cross-check (2026-10-01): diverges from the released code on junction angles, bond stiffness (6.0 vs 100), break mechanism and stretch protocol; treat σ(ε̇) as exploratory until re-run. See references/cross-check-vs-released-code.md.
Clean-room parameters transcribed from the spec; the authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515) and not yet cross-checked against this build.
σ(ε̇) is elastic-dominated at these rates; the viscous plateau is not yet resolved.
Crosslink count differs across rates, confounding σ(ε̇).
Same small-network / noise caveats as stage 1.

report.title: Stage 2 — σ(ε̇) on the growing substrate
report.verdict: Produces the investigation's coupling deliverable: from the faithful, density-calibrated model, the effective modulus E(ε̇) (≈7→11 Pa, stiffening with growth rate) and the remodelling time τ(ε̇) (≈36–51 τ, roughly constant) tabulated vs growth rate — the two numbers the AICS vertex model takes in the offline coupling. Absolute Pa still depends on the energy-scale decision (#4).
report.main_insight: The clean-room network is stiff/elastic on the sampled timescales — remodelling is too slow relative to the imposed strain to give a viscous plateau yet.
